Reflection, Blueprint exposure and native creation

Expose tuning and observation deliberately; reflection metadata is not a security boundary.

On this page
Native creationExposure tableLifetime and threading

Native creation

For a new Actor-derived class, the public5.8 tutorial uses Tools > New C++ Class, choose Actor/Character or Show All Classes as appropriate, name the native class without an A/U prefix in the wizard, then inspect generated native declarations in the IDE. For a custom movement default subobject, reflected struct, interface or backend adapter, use the appropriate native file/type workflow and existing module rather than inventing a Blueprint factory.

Close/rebuild the Editor after reflected layout changes when necessary; do not rely on a stale hot-reloaded class to validate serialized Blueprint properties. The exact toolchain and live coding behavior must be tested in the installed environment. Create a Blueprint child only after the native parent successfully appears in the class picker.

Lifetime and threading

Use reflected strong references for owned Unreal objects that must survive garbage collection and weak handles for asynchronous observers that may disappear. HTTP/DB callbacks must marshal updates to the appropriate game-thread/native owner and verify request generation, CharacterId and epoch before applying. Do not mutate UObject state from an arbitrary worker callback.

World teardown cancels timers/tasks, unregisters delegates and marks pending callbacks invalid. A successful backend receipt remains durable even if the local observer disappeared; next snapshot resolves it. No callback should resurrect an old pawn or old screen after travel.
